candidates.rationale: Weakness: monotone IC decay across the fit window, +0.0250 in 2000 falling to +0.0027 in 2012 and +0.0010 in 2013, while turnover and coverage are fine. The fast component is the spot-price numerator; the 21-day range frame in the denominator still works as a volatility scale. Replacing the numerator anchor with a 126-day mean price asks a slow question (where the half-year average sits inside the recent range) instead of a same-day stochastic reading, which also moves the shape out of the pure range-position template that has been losing proposals.

Weakness: stability 0.86, with the sign flipping in 2003 (-0.0051) and 2013 (-0.0013), both low-volatility trending years. The culprit is the second correlation argument: $high - $low enters as a dollar level, so inside a trending 21-day window it co-trends with volume for price-drift reasons rather than information reasons, and that spurious component is what inverts in quiet years. Scaling the range by the same-day raw open makes the correlation about relative range and keeps both series on the raw OHLC scale, so no adjusted/raw mixing. Correlation is scale invariant, so a slow volume normalizer would have been a no-op here; the change has to be on the range argument.

candidates.changed_node: right leg CS_RANK(...) wrapped in CS_DEMEAN
candidates.rationale: Weakness: |rho| 0.710 against archived RANK($roa), close to the 0.80 gate, so the factor is mostly a re-weighted profitability rank. The responsible node is the volatility leg's CS_RANK, which is strictly positive and therefore only rescales the ROE tilt without ever reordering it. Demeaning that leg makes the product a genuine two-sided interaction that flips sign for the calm half of the universe, which is what breaks the collinearity with the archived ROA factor while keeping the 57-day half-life and 0.029 turnover intact. Depth goes to 6, at the cap.

candidates.changed_node: price-leg anchor TS_MIN($low, 21) replaced by TS_MEAN($low, 126)
candidates.rationale: Weakness: turnover 0.134 one-way, the highest of the fundamental-anchored parents, paired with a 17.6-day half-life; the ROA leg turns over at 0.007, so all the churn comes from the price leg's 21-day extreme anchor, which jumps whenever a single new low prints. Replacing TS_MIN($low, 21) with TS_MEAN($low, 126) turns that leg into the price's distance above its half-year support level: it moves slowly, so the position stops paying for extreme-value noise, and it puts the leg in the medium/slow window band where this island's accepts live.

candidates.changed_node: volatility leg TS_STD($return, 126) replaced by TS_STD($return, 21) / (TS_STD($return, 126) + 1e-8)
candidates.rationale: Weakness: stability 0.86 with a late-sample fade, 2010 +0.0016 and 2013 -0.0045, against strong early years. The 189-day position leg is the part that held up; the weak node is CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 126)), a level-of-volatility rank, which is a persistent cross-sectional characteristic whose payoff inverts with the low-volatility regime and drags the whole product with it. Swapping the level for short-over-long volatility makes that leg a mean-reverting state variable (is this name expanding or contracting relative to its own six-month norm) rather than a static high-beta bet. Coverage is unchanged at 189 days, so the 0.904 margin does not move.

Weakness: as a raw level, $volume is a size and liquidity proxy, which is why it sits at |rho| 0.717 against archived TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21), and why it pays 0.153 one-way turnover on a signal whose IC half-life exceeds 63 days: the daily noise reshuffles positions without changing the underlying slow ranking. The only node is the leaf, so it is replaced by its own relative form. The ratio is scale free, which removes the size exposure driving the archive correlation, and both legs are averages, which cuts the churn. Volume enters as a 126-day-referenced measure rather than a same-day one.

Weakness: |rho| 0.737 against an archived ROA combination, the highest archive correlation of any parent, plus negative years in 2003 (-0.0045) and 2006 (-0.0026), the junk-rally years where a static profitability level is on the wrong side. The weak node is the $roa leaf itself: it is a level, so it carries no timing and duplicates what the archive already spans. Taking its change over 126 trading days, roughly two report stamps, converts it to profitability improvement, a distinct signal from the level, and keeps turnover near zero because the field only moves on report dates.

candidates.changed_node: numerator anchors DELAY($close, 21) and DELAY($close, 147) replaced by TS_MEAN($close, 21) and TS_MEAN($close, 147)
candidates.rationale: Weakness: IC half-life 3.1 days, by far the shortest here, on a signal built from prices that are 21 and 147 days old. The numerator anchor pair is responsible: two single daily closes carry each day's idiosyncratic noise, and the DELAY(21) skip means the reading is a month stale before it is ever traded. Replacing both anchors with means over the same spans makes the numerator a current, smoothed trend measure (21-day average against the 147-day average) so the horizon matches the decay, while the 105-day volatility denominator is left untouched.

Weakness: turnover 0.177 one-way, the highest of all parents, on the lowest IC (0.00572) and a 4.9-day half-life, and |rho| 0.706 against another archived accrual-times-daily-range factor. All three trace to the same node: the numerator is a single day's range, pure session noise. Averaging it over 21 days makes the leg a volatility level rather than a daily print, so the ratio reads as the drawdown from the 21-day high measured in typical daily ranges. The signal slows down, the cost drops, and it separates from the archived version, which is built from 2-day and 5-day ranges.

Weakness: stability 0.71, the worst here, with four negative years clustered at 2007 (-0.0002), 2009 (-0.0027), 2010 (-0.0018) and 2011 (-0.0030). The quality leg is not the problem: the archived profitability rank is strongly positive in exactly 2007 and 2008. The failing node is the book-to-price numerator, since book value is the accounting quantity that breaks through a credit cycle and reprices with a lag. Swapping the stock for the flow keeps the value idea and the same raw price denominator (no adjusted/raw mixing) while pricing current earnings, which is the version that does not invert for four straight years.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.
